# full_member pseudo-perm + guest member marker

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-08-01
- **Requested by**: Ian — serves Maestro-workspace item [#1131 "Workspace member roles — Admin / Member / Guest"](https://maestromojo.com/workspaces/#/board/8?item=1131) (imported via its child [#1132](https://maestromojo.com/workspaces/#/board/8?item=1132); supersedes duplicate NativeMojo filing #1133, archived). This item owns ONLY the framework primitive; every app-side enforcement point, role action, invite path, and UI belongs to the upstream plan.

Apply rules: `django-mojo-build-conventions`, `nativemojo-board-conventions`.

## Description

A `GroupMember` row can carry a guest marker (`permissions["guest"] = True`), and permission checks gain a `"full_member"` pseudo-perm that guests fail while ordinary membership checks (`"member"`, `"all"`, `"authenticated"`) still pass for them. The marker's absence means full member — nothing changes for any existing member row. Ships as a PyPI release so the consuming app can pin a version floor on it.

## Context

The upstream workspace-roles feature needs the framework to tell a full member from a view-only guest. Semantics: `"member"` stays "any member row" (view tier); `"full_member"` is the write tier — a member row not marked guest. The marker is set/cleared via the existing `add_permission("guest")` / `remove_permission("guest")`; `can_change_permission` gates writes to the marker at manage level (or per `MEMBER_PERMS_PROTECTION`).

**Contract the challenge sharpened (must be documented, and upstream must honor it): marking guest does not strip or freeze the row's other grants.** A row `{"guest": true, "manage_group": true}` still passes any tier that ORs in `manage_group` — including the gate that would let it clear its own marker. Demotion = strip manage-level grants **and** set the marker. A plain guest (marker only, no other grants) cannot clear its own flag.

**Release ordering**: the upstream build is blocked until this is on PyPI — publish-before-deploy is the only ordering to honor. Upstream pins its dependency floor to whatever version ships.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `GroupMember.has_permission("full_member")` is True for a plain member row, False while `permissions["guest"]` is truthy, True again after `remove_permission("guest")`.
- [ ] Guests still satisfy `"member"` (and `"all"`/`"authenticated"`) — the view tier is untouched.
- [ ] List-OR works: `has_permission(["full_member"])` behaves like the scalar form.
- [ ] `ApiKey.has_permission` and `User.has_permission` are deliberately NOT changed. `"full_member"` fails closed on both (explicit grant or superuser only). Docs record the pre-existing asymmetry that a key passes the `"member"` view tier unconditionally (`api_key.py:212`) — keys are NOT "not members" for view-tier purposes.
- [ ] The resolution seam behaves: `Group.user_has_permission(user, ["full_member"])` is True for a plain member, False for a guest, False for a non-member non-superuser, True for a superuser, and True for a guest holding an explicit **global** `full_member` grant (global dict short-circuits at `group.py:213` — documented as override semantics).
- [ ] Framework tests cover the above; docs updated in both tracks incl. the guest≠demotion contract; released to PyPI before the upstream deploy.

## Investigation

- **What exists**:
  - `mojo/apps/account/models/member.py::has_permission` (line 116) — list-OR recursion at the top, `sys.`-prefix delegation to `User.has_permission`, the `["all", "authenticated", "member"]` special case (line 135), then the `implied_perms` dict lookup (line 139). `add_permission` / `remove_permission` (141–154) write the `permissions` JSONField and leave every other key untouched. `can_change_permission` (84–103) restricts permission writes to manage-level requesters (line 102: `manage_group`, `manage_members`, `manage_users`, `manage_groups`) or per `MEMBER_PERMS_PROTECTION` (100–101).
  - `mojo/helpers/perms.py::implied_perms` — expands only `view_`/`manage_` forms of the seven domain categories; every other key passes through as `(perm_key,)`. Without a dedicated branch, `"full_member"` would be an ordinary grantable stored perm defaulting False.
  - `mojo/apps/account/models/api_key.py::has_permission` (189) — `"member"` is always True for a key (212–213), `sys.*` always False, everything else reads the key's own permissions dict → `"full_member"` on a key is False unless explicitly granted. Fail closed, explicit opt-in possible.
  - `mojo/apps/account/models/user.py::has_permission` (572) — superuser bypass first (574), then the platform-wide dict (585) → `"full_member"` False for non-superusers unless explicitly granted globally.
  - `mojo/apps/account/models/group.py::user_has_permission` (212–220) — **global dict first** (213), then the member row (217–219). Consequences: a bare `["full_member"]` list denies platform operators with no member row; a stored global `full_member` grant short-circuits before the member row and overrides the guest marker in every group.
  - **Clean namespace**: zero occurrences of `full_member` and zero Python uses of a `guest` permission in `mojo/`, `tests/`, `docs/`.

- **What changes**: one early-return branch in `GroupMember.has_permission`, docstring, tests, docs, release prep. No model/schema change — no migration, no `bin/create_testproject`.
- **Constraints**:
  - `has_permission` is row-local and does NOT consult `is_active` — existing behavior; activeness is enforced by the lookup paths. Settled upstream; do NOT add an activeness test.
  - List-OR needs no code — the recursion at the top covers it.

## Plan

### Objective

`GroupMember.has_permission("full_member")` returns True exactly when the row is not marked guest; everything else about membership checks is byte-for-byte unchanged. Shipped as django-mojo 1.2.65 (release commit + tag prepared; Ian publishes).

### Implementation steps

1. **`mojo/apps/account/models/member.py`** — in `has_permission`, immediately after the `["all", "authenticated", "member"]` special case and before the `implied_perms` lookup (anchor on the list literal, not line numbers), add:

   ```python
   if perm_key == "full_member":
       return not bool(self.permissions.get("guest", False))
   ```

   Extend the method docstring with the tier pair and its contract: `"member"` = any member row (view tier); `"full_member"` = member row not marked guest (write tier); the marker is `permissions["guest"]`, set/cleared via `add_permission("guest")` / `remove_permission("guest")` under the `can_change_permission` gate; a stored `permissions["full_member"]` key is ignored on member rows (derived, not grantable — D1); **marking guest does not strip or freeze other grants — demotion = strip grants + set marker** (a plain guest cannot clear its own flag; one still holding `manage_group` can).

2. **Tests** — new `tests/test_account/test_member_full_member.py`, style mirroring `test_group_save_perms.py` (module-level `_mk_user` helper, `@th.django_unit_setup()` with delete-before-create on a unique prefix, ORM-level `Group.add_member` + `GroupMember` fetch; no REST client — see Challenge #4). Read `docs/django_developer/testit/Overview.md` first per `.claude/rules/testing.md`. Tests (every assert with a failure message):
   - plain member row: `"full_member"` True; `"member"`, `"all"`, `"authenticated"` all True.
   - after `add_permission("guest")`: `"full_member"` False; `"member"`/`"all"`/`"authenticated"` still True.
   - after `remove_permission("guest")`: `"full_member"` True again.
   - list-OR: `["full_member"]` matches the scalar in both states; mixed list `["manage_group", "full_member"]` is True for a guest row holding `manage_group` (OR semantics — this doubles as the guest≠demotion contract made executable).
   - spoof-resistance: a guest row with `permissions["full_member"] = True` written directly still fails `"full_member"`.
   - falsy-marker edge: `permissions["guest"] = False` present-but-falsy → `"full_member"` True.
   - **resolution seam** (`Group.user_has_permission`, the path REST perm lists actually take): `["full_member"]` → plain member True; guest False; non-member non-superuser False; superuser True; guest with explicit global `full_member` grant True (global short-circuit, override semantics).

3. **Docs, django track** — `docs/django_developer/account/group.md`, "GroupMember Model" section (after the member-level-permissions snippet, ~line 301): a "Membership tiers" block covering — the member/full_member pair; the guest marker and who may set it (`can_change_permission`, tunable per-key via `MEMBER_PERMS_PROTECTION`, e.g. `{"guest": ["manage_groups"]}` to raise the bar); derived-not-grantable on member rows; **guest ≠ demotion** (strip grants + set marker; self-clear consequence when manage grants remain); the `ApiKey` asymmetry (`"member"` unconditionally True for keys; `"full_member"` explicit grant only); `User` behavior (superuser bypass; a stored **global** `full_member` grant short-circuits before the member row and overrides the marker in every group); composition guidance (write tiers should be `["manage_group", ..., "full_member"]`-shaped — a bare `["full_member"]` locks out platform operators without member rows).

4. **Docs, web track** — `docs/web_developer/account/group.md`, under "Update Member Permissions" (~line 162): saving a member with `{"permissions": {"guest": true}}` marks a view-only guest (requires manage-level perms); `"full_member"` is then usable in permission lists to gate write-tier access; clearing restores full membership; **demoting an existing manager also requires removing their manage grants** — the marker alone does not.

5. **Release prep** (after implementation commit is green): bump `pyproject.toml` to `1.2.65`, commit `Release v1.2.65` (explicit pathspec; CHANGELOG untouched), tag `v1.2.65`. **Stop there** — `git push` and the PyPI upload are Ian's manual steps. Before the release commit, run the pre-publish gate: `bin/run_tests --agent --full`.

### Design decisions

- **D1 — early-return makes `full_member` derived-only on member rows.** Placed before the `implied_perms` lookup, a stored `permissions["full_member"]` key is ignored: through the `full_member` key itself, the only way a member row passes the write tier is not being marked guest. Honest limit (from Challenge #1): this invariant holds only for the `full_member` key — the marker does not strip or freeze *other* grants, so real-world tiers ORing in `manage_*` still pass for a marked row that retains those grants. Demotion policy (strip + mark) is the consumer's job and is documented, not enforced — auto-stripping on `add_permission("guest")` was considered and rejected (destructive surprise inside a generic permission setter; KISS).
- **D2 — truthiness, not presence.** `not bool(...get("guest", False))` — any truthy value marks guest; present-but-falsy means full member. Matches the method's existing idiom.
- **D3 — `ApiKey`/`User`/`Group.user_has_permission` untouched, verified.** Keys: `"full_member"` fails closed, explicit per-key opt-in possible; the pre-existing `"member"`-always-True asymmetry is documented, not changed. Users: superuser bypass; a global `full_member` grant is an intentional platform-operator override and short-circuits ahead of the member row (`group.py:213`) — documented as override semantics and pinned by a seam test.
- **D4 — no `is_active` consult** — settled upstream; re-litigating would change `"member"` semantics for every consumer.
- **D5 — `full_member` is NOT a domain category.** No `view_`/`manage_` expansion; `mojo/helpers/perms.py` untouched.
- **D6 — release prepared in-session, published by Ian.** Matches the `Release vX.Y.Z` + tag pattern; no publish CI; credentials never pass through the agent.
- **D7 — baseline scope follows `build-baseline.md` as it stands at build time.** If #1094's scoped rule has landed: baseline + verify on `test_account`, `test_global_perms`, `test_auth` (`bin/run_tests --agent -t <module>`). If the old whole-suite rule is still in force: whole suite before and after. The `--full` release gate runs before the release commit either way.

### Edge cases and error handling

- Truthy guest variants (`1`, `"yes"`) → guest; present-but-falsy → full member (D2, tested).
- `sys.full_member` → delegates to `User.has_permission("full_member")` — existing `sys.` semantics.
- Non-member (no row) → resolution paths fail closed before reaching the member method (tested at the seam).
- Inactive member/group rows → per-marker answer like every other perm; activeness stays the lookup paths' job (D4).
- Guest marker rides the already-exposed `permissions` field in the default member graph — no new serialization exposure (challenge-verified).
- No REST surface changes; `"full_member"` in a RestMeta perms list flows through `Group.user_has_permission` / member resolution (challenge-traced: `rest.py` → `group.py:212-220` → member row).

### Challenge

Independent red-team (fresh context, read access, full trace from RestMeta perm lists to the member row and every write path to `GroupMember.permissions`). Verdict: no exploitable hole; four objections, all dispositioned; every disposition re-verified in-repo by the scoping session.

1. **"Guest is a marker, not a demotion — D1's rationale overclaims, and a guest retaining `manage_group` passes write tiers and can clear its own marker."** — **amended.** Verified: `add_permission` (member.py:141-148) leaves other keys untouched; `can_change_permission` line 102 admits `manage_group`; OR-composed tiers pass. No framework escalation (the row legitimately holds the grant), but the "set guest ⇒ view-only" assumption would silently ship write-tier guests upstream. Plan now: docstring + both doc tracks state **demotion = strip grants + set marker**; the mixed-list test makes the contract executable; D1 rewritten to claim only what it delivers; `MEMBER_PERMS_PROTECTION` documented as the knob to raise who may touch the marker; upstream #1132 notified (their enforcement plan owns demotion). Auto-strip on marking rejected — destructive surprise inside a generic setter.
2. **"AC bullet 4 is wrong: keys DO pass the view tier — `'member'` is unconditionally True for an ApiKey."** — **amended.** Verified api_key.py:212-213. AC reworded; the asymmetry goes in the django-track docs. Only `"full_member"` fails closed on keys.
3. **"Composition footgun in both directions: bare `['full_member']` locks out platform operators; a stored global `full_member` grant short-circuits ahead of the member row and defeats the marker."** — **amended.** Verified group.py:212-220 (global dict first, line 213). Both directions documented (step 3) and pinned by seam tests; the global grant is accepted as intentional operator-override semantics (D3), not closed off.
4. **"The integration seam is asserted, never tested — add one REST-level test."** — **partially amended.** Adopted at the `Group.user_has_permission` level (the seam REST perm lists actually traverse — challenge's own trace), giving five seam assertions incl. the global-override case. A literal REST-endpoint test is rebutted: no shipped `RestMeta` uses `full_member` yet, and mutating a model's `RestMeta` from a test is the exact global-state race #1072 closed. The endpoint-level pin belongs to upstream's integration suite where a real consumer surface exists.

Attacked and held (challenger's own verification, spot-checked): plain-guest self-clear blocked twice (`SAVE_PERMS` gate then per-key `can_change_permission`); invite/add_member paths never touch an existing row's permissions; spoofed stored `full_member` inert (branch precedes the dict lookup); `implied_perms` passthrough exact; no new serialization exposure (marker rides the already-exposed `permissions` field); docs anchors exist — web-track anchor corrected to "Update Member Permissions" (~line 162).
